section_summary: The section begins with Japanese thanks for American vessels that assisted distressed crews, followed by reports of a collision and a fishing boat rescue near Nagasaki. Most of the pages concern the wrecked Kowa Maru and whether Japanese vessels could conduct salvage in Philippine waters. State Department, War Department, naval, and diplomatic correspondence examines territorial waters, port access, Philippine regulations, and Japan’s claim of reciprocal salvage rights.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Japanese thanks to the Wisconsin
subfiles.about: Requests delivery of Japanese thanks to Captain Peterson for towing the Daihachi Ume Maru into Hakodate.
subfiles.summary: The Tokyo embassy forwards a Japanese Foreign Office note praising the Wisconsin’s assistance to a distressed Japanese steamer.

subfiles.title: Japanese Foreign Office note thanking Captain Peterson
subfiles.about: Thanks the Wisconsin’s captain for assisting and towing the Daihachi Ume Maru.
subfiles.summary: Japan asks that its thanks be conveyed to Captain E. Peterson.

subfiles.title: Handwritten routing advice on conveying thanks
subfiles.about: Suggests sending the Japanese expression of thanks through the Commerce Department.
subfiles.summary: A handwritten note favors Commerce as the channel for conveying thanks to the ship’s captain.

subfiles.title: Request to Commerce to convey Japanese thanks
subfiles.about: Asks Commerce to transmit Japan’s thanks to the Wisconsin’s captain.
subfiles.summary: The Department forwards copies of the embassy despatch and note and requests delivery of the message to Captain Peterson.

subfiles.title: Document file note on Japanese rescue thanks
subfiles.about: Indexes correspondence concerning Japanese thanks for assistance by an American ship.
subfiles.summary: An index note points to related rescue correspondence.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Japanese thanks for attempted Siyo Maru rescue
subfiles.about: Forwards a Japanese note thanking an American vessel for attempting to rescue the Siyo Maru near the Aleutian Islands.
subfiles.summary: The embassy sends the note for transmission to the Americans concerned.

subfiles.title: Japanese note on the Siyo Maru rescue attempt
subfiles.about: Thanks the captain and crew of a vessel that searched for the sinking Siyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: The note praises efforts made in heavy seas to locate the distressed Japanese steamer.

subfiles.title: File note on the Suwa Maru crew rescue
subfiles.about: Indexes Japanese thanks to the President McKinley for rescuing the Suwa Maru crew.
subfiles.summary: The note refers to the related embassy despatch.

subfiles.title: Embassy transmittal of thanks to the President McKinley
subfiles.about: Forwards Japan’s request to thank the President McKinley’s captain and crew for rescuing nine fishermen.
subfiles.summary: The rescued crew was carried to Honolulu; the embassy requests that the Japanese message be conveyed through appropriate channels.

subfiles.title: Japanese note thanking the President McKinley
subfiles.about: Requests delivery of Japan’s thanks for rescuing nine fishermen and taking them to Honolulu.
subfiles.summary: The note recounts the fishing vessel’s storm damage and the American ship’s rescue.

subfiles.title: Embassy acknowledgment of Japanese rescue note
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Japan’s thanks and promises to forward the message.
subfiles.summary: The embassy will ask the State Department to convey the note to the American ship’s crew.

subfiles.title: File note on wrecked Japanese vessel
subfiles.about: Indexes a related record concerning a wrecked Japanese vessel.
subfiles.summary: A brief file note points to another wreck record.

subfiles.title: Foreign Service Administration note on Nagasaki
subfiles.about: Comments on a recommendation to close the Nagasaki consulate and on rescue reporting.
subfiles.summary: Olsson recalls no closure recommendation or papers and says foreign seamen’s rescues are outside his direct work.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs routing note on the Birmingham City
subfiles.about: Flags a rescue despatch and its bearing on the proposed closure of the Nagasaki consulate.
subfiles.summary: The note highlights that the Birmingham City was the first American steamer to call since March 1933.

subfiles.title: Rescue of the No. 8 Sumiyoshi Maru crew
subfiles.about: Reports the Birmingham City’s rescue of Japanese fishermen near Nagasaki.
subfiles.summary: After the fishing boat struck a rock near Hashima, the Birmingham City and Kofuku Maru rescued ten survivors; one later died. The consul forwards thanks and notes the ship’s rare Nagasaki call.

subfiles.title: Telegrams thanking the Birmingham City
subfiles.from: Tokushima Ken Fishing Association; Shintaro Nagasaka
subfiles.about: Conveys thanks for rescuing people from the No. 8 Sumiyoshi Maru.
subfiles.summary: The association and boat owner send separate messages of gratitude.

subfiles.title: Governor’s thanks for the Nagasaki rescue
subfiles.about: Reports the Nagasaki governor’s formal thanks to Captain Green and his crew.
subfiles.summary: The consul encloses a translation of the governor’s letter and his request to the ship company to deliver it.

subfiles.title: Nagasaki governor’s letter to the Birmingham City
subfiles.to: Captain B. M. Green and crew
subfiles.about: Thanks the ship’s crew for rescuing survivors of the wrecked No. 8 Sumiyoshi Maru.
subfiles.summary: The governor describes oil used to calm the water and the crew’s launch rescue in heavy seas.

subfiles.title: Forwarding the governor’s letter to Captain Green
subfiles.about: Requests delivery of the Nagasaki governor’s letter and translation to Captain Green.
subfiles.summary: The consul encloses the governor’s thanks for forwarding to the ship’s master.

subfiles.title: Kobe telegram on the Midori Maru disaster
subfiles.about: Reports the Midori Maru’s sinking after a collision and the absence of foreign passengers.
subfiles.summary: The telegram also reports no American casualties in recent Kobe, Osaka, and Kyoto floods.

subfiles.title: Second copy of the Kobe disaster telegram
subfiles.about: Repeats the report of the Midori Maru collision and regional floods.
subfiles.summary: A second copy of the same telegram records no foreign passengers or American flood casualties.

subfiles.title: Interim instruction concerning Morita’s wreck inspection
subfiles.about: Records interim advice not to authorize Morita to inspect the Kowa Maru pending a decision.
subfiles.summary: The note quotes a July 24 message to High Commissioner McNutt.

subfiles.title: War Department transmittal of Kowa Maru papers
subfiles.about: Forwards correspondence and a radiogram about the stranded Kowa Maru.
subfiles.summary: The War Department offers to radio State’s response to the High Commissioner.

subfiles.title: High Commissioner’s request for advice
subfiles.about: Requests State and War Department advice on a Japanese plan to float or dismantle the Kowa Maru.
subfiles.summary: Coy forwards Japanese and naval correspondence and notes that the wreck’s location governs whether the United States may object.

subfiles.title: Japanese consul’s notice of proposed Kowa Maru salvage
subfiles.about: Gives notice of Masuichi Morita’s plan to float or dismantle the stranded ship.
subfiles.summary: Uchiyama says the wreck lies in open sea near Balabac and encloses a picture.

subfiles.title: Diagram enclosed with the Kowa Maru correspondence
subfiles.about: Shows numbered sections and measurements associated with the wreck.
subfiles.summary: A diagram records structural measurements.

subfiles.title: Naval assessment of the Kowa Maru salvage proposal
subfiles.about: Questions the wreck’s claimed open sea location and warns against foreign salvage operations.
subfiles.summary: Meyers places the wreck within three miles of Gnat Reef, raising a territorial waters issue. He also warns that foreign crews might use closed ports and survey the area.

subfiles.title: Survey description of the Kowa Maru wreck
subfiles.from: U.S. Coast and Geodetic Survey, Manila Field Station
subfiles.about: Describes the Kowa Maru’s position and physical condition on Southwestern Bank.
subfiles.summary: The coal laden wreck is waterlogged, rusted, and stripped of movable fittings.

subfiles.title: High Commissioner’s acknowledgment to Uchiyama
subfiles.about: Says the proposed Kowa Maru salvage is being referred to Washington.
subfiles.summary: Coy promises an answer when State Department advice arrives.

subfiles.title: McNutt radiogram on Morita’s inspection request
subfiles.about: Asks urgently whether Morita may inspect the wreck while a salvage decision remains pending.
subfiles.summary: Morita has arrived in Manila and seeks to visit the Kowa Maru.

subfiles.title: State Department advice on Kowa Maru salvage
subfiles.about: Sets out legal and policy considerations for Japanese salvage of the Kowa Maru.
subfiles.summary: State finds no applicable United States treaty or law. If the wreck is in Philippine waters, local law and policy govern; possible conditions include American or Philippine vessel availability, Japanese reciprocity, and restrictions on closed ports. State recommends seeking Navy Department views.

subfiles.title: Dickover memorandum on treaties and salvage
subfiles.about: Considers whether treaty provisions could support a Japanese claim to salvage rights.
subfiles.summary: Dickover discusses the disputed position of the wreck and suggests that the 1911 United States–Japan most favored nation clause might extend a salvage privilege granted to Britain. He asks whether Japan’s reciprocal practice must be established before refusing its request.

subfiles.title: Legal Adviser opinion on the treaty argument
subfiles.about: Rejects application of the 1911 treaty’s commerce and navigation clause to salvage.
subfiles.summary: The opinion finds the British treaty geographically limited and salvage distinct from ordinary commerce and navigation. It reviews treaty drafting and concludes that Philippine law or policy should govern. It suggests considering reciprocity and whether an American salvage boat is available.

subfiles.title: Note on Philippine salvage proclamation
subfiles.about: Reports a Philippine proclamation favoring American and Philippine salvage vessels.
subfiles.summary: Dickover links the proclamation to the Kowa Maru case.

subfiles.title: War Department forwards Philippine salvage order
subfiles.about: Forwards Philippine Executive Order No. 123 on salvage work.
subfiles.summary: The War Department notes that State’s earlier advice was sent to the High Commissioner.

subfiles.title: Coy transmittal of Executive Order No. 123
subfiles.about: Sends the Philippine salvage order for State Department information and comment.
subfiles.summary: Coy requests that the order be forwarded to State.

subfiles.title: Philippine Executive Order No. 123
subfiles.about: Regulates salvage permits, vessel registry, port access, and reciprocity in the Philippines.
subfiles.summary: The order favors available American and Philippine vessels and conditions foreign salvage on reciprocity, except in emergencies.

subfiles.title: War Department forwards McNutt’s reciprocity query
subfiles.about: Forwards a High Commissioner radiogram on Japanese salvage reciprocity.
subfiles.summary: The War Department offers to relay State’s response.

subfiles.title: McNutt radiogram quoting Japanese reciprocity assurance
subfiles.about: Asks whether Japan’s stated reciprocal salvage policy satisfies United States requirements.
subfiles.summary: McNutt quotes Consul General Uchiyama’s assurance, then contrasts it with reported exclusion of American salvage firms after the President Hoover grounded.

subfiles.title: State reply on Japanese salvage applications
subfiles.about: Provides a proposed reply to McNutt on Japan’s request for reciprocal salvage rights.
subfiles.summary: State says a continuing reciprocal arrangement belongs in diplomatic channels. Individual applications should be judged under Executive Order No. 123; confidentially, it recommends refusing foreign applications outside emergencies while Japan’s practice is investigated.

subfiles.title: Confidential instruction to investigate Japanese salvage practice
subfiles.about: Requests discreet inquiries into whether Japan actually permits reciprocal foreign salvage.
subfiles.summary: The Department recounts Japan’s reciprocity assurance and Philippine Executive Order No. 123. It asks the embassy to examine the different treatment of the President Hoover and Netherlands tanker Angelina off Formosa before accepting Japan’s stated policy.

subfiles.title: File note on the President Hoover stranding
subfiles.about: Points to a report that a Japanese tug refused to assist the stranded President Hoover.
subfiles.summary: The note cites a claim that the ship lay in restricted naval waters.

subfiles.title: Dickover draft response on salvage reciprocity
subfiles.about: Seeks comments on a proposed response to McNutt about Japanese salvage privileges.
subfiles.summary: The draft weighs the President Hoover refusal against the Angelina towing and proposes judging Japanese applications individually under Philippine rules and reciprocal conditions.

subfiles.title: Copy of Philippine Executive Order No. 123
subfiles.about: Repeats the Philippine rules governing salvage permits and foreign vessels.
subfiles.summary: The order requires permits and limits foreign salvage according to availability, port access, and reciprocity.

subfiles.title: Legal Adviser request for evidence of Japanese practice
subfiles.about: Urges more evidence before accepting Japan’s asserted reciprocal salvage policy.
subfiles.summary: The Angelina case might represent either general practice or a special exception.

subfiles.title: Philippine Affairs routing request
subfiles.about: Requests policy direction on action following the Tokyo salvage despatch.
subfiles.summary: The office seeks instructions while Mr. Jacobs is absent.

subfiles.title: Embassy report on Japanese salvage reciprocity
subfiles.about: Reports an investigation of Japan’s claimed reciprocal salvage policy.
subfiles.summary: The embassy finds that military and naval restrictions would likely prevent foreign salvage in most Japanese waters, despite the consul’s assurance. It contrasts the limited towing of Angelina with the refusal of foreign participation in the President Hoover salvage, and discusses Japanese work on the Asama Maru at Hong Kong. No Japanese law expressly bars foreign salvage, but no affirmative reciprocal right was found.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs recommendation after embassy report
subfiles.about: Recommends continued refusal of routine Japanese salvage applications in Philippine waters.
subfiles.summary: The division concludes that Japan’s reciprocal assurance is unlikely to work in practice because of military restrictions and the President Hoover precedent. It also sees an imbalance between Japanese salvage capacity and Philippine access to Japanese waters.

subfiles.title: State instruction to continue refusing routine Japanese salvage requests
subfiles.about: Asks War to send confidential salvage guidance to the High Commissioner.
subfiles.summary: State advises generally refusing Japanese salvage applications in Philippine waters because reciprocal access for American and Philippine vessels has not been shown. Each case remains subject to individual judgment.

subfiles.title: Reported sinking of the Taiyo
subfiles.about: Reports a collision between the Japanese tuna boat Taiyo and American boat Dependable near Cabo San Lucas.
subfiles.summary: The Taiyo reportedly sank on July 17, 1938. Its crew was taken to San Lucas, and no lives were reported lost.

subfiles.title: War Department forwards further Kowa Maru correspondence
subfiles.about: Forwards a June 28 letter and enclosures from the High Commissioner on Kowa Maru salvage.
subfiles.summary: The War Department submits further Philippine correspondence for State’s consideration.

subfiles.title: McNutt’s further report on the Kowa Maru proposal
subfiles.about: Reports further Japanese correspondence and a Philippine discussion of who determines salvage boat availability.
subfiles.summary: McNutt says the Japanese consul’s March letter remains unanswered. He and President Quezon agreed that Philippine officials would determine whether American or Philippine salvage boats are available, and he forwards additional Commonwealth correspondence for comment.
